items.claim: The addressee-specific messenger-formula oracle against the royal steward is correctly bounded at both edges by genuine frame shifts, not by a weaker signal.
items.evidence: Isa.22.15 opens on כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָא֑וֹת לֶךְ בֹּא֙ אֶל הַסֹּכֵ֣ן הַזֶּ֔ה עַל שֶׁבְנָ֖א אֲשֶׁ֥ר עַל הַבָּֽיִת naming the steward alone as addressee, distinct from the first-person revelation report closing at Isa.22.14 on the parallel signature אָמַ֛ר אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת; the row's own close before Isa.22.20's fresh in-that-day onset marks a real addressee turn (the steward's removal is complete; a different named servant is introduced next). The rejected alternative (merging with the installation oracle) is a genuine live rival, not a strawman, since both share the messenger formula's larger frame.

items.claim: The installation sub-unit is correctly launched on its own in-that-day frame onset, and the servant language is properly scoped to a named referent.
items.evidence: Isa.22.20 opens on וְהָיָ֖ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֑וּא וְקָרָ֣אתִי לְעַבְדִּ֔י לְאֶלְיָקִ֖ים בֶּן חִלְקִיָּֽהוּ, the same bayom-hahu scene-turn device the chapter also uses at Isa.22.12 and Isa.22.25; the row correctly keeps this named-referent servant mention apart from the book's unnamed servant-figure zones. Its disclosed merge rival is genuine, though its stated ground (shared addressee) is weaker than the strongest available textual warrant for that rival.

items.claim: The row's own case for standing apart from the installation material omits the strongest cross-seam cohesion evidence: a byte-identical catchword phrase binding its opening verse to the installation verse it separates from.
items.evidence: Isa.22.23's peg-clause and Isa.22.25's peg-clause share the phrase בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן / בְּמָק֣וֹם נֶאֱמָ֑ן at the byte tier, cantillation included, plus the shared root behind וּתְקַעְתִּ֥יו and הַתְּקוּעָ֖ה ('fasten'/'driven'), forming a deliberate installed-then-dislodged bracket around the peg image that straddles this row's own opening seam. The row's disclosed merge rival names only a generic ground ('the same figure is in view across both verses'), not this verbatim catchword, which is the exact class of undisclosed byte-true device the lens is built to catch. This does not overturn the boundary itself, since the fresh in-that-day-plus-neum onset at Isa.22.25 remains a real, independent frame signal; the defect is the missing disclosure of the countervailing device, not a wrong division.

items.claim: The refrain bracket closing this row is a verified accent-stripped-tier match to its own opening cry, correctly argued as the stronger closing signal over the finer internal splits the row considers and rejects.
items.evidence: The howl-ships-of-Tarshish cry at Isa.23.1 (הֵילִ֣ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֗ישׁ) and at Isa.23.14 (הֵילִ֖ילוּ אֳנִיּ֣וֹת תַּרְשִׁ֑ישׁ) match at the consonant-and-vowel-point (accent-stripped) tier, with cantillation differing only; checked directly against the source bytes, the two are NOT byte-identical, and the row correctly names the accent-stripped tier rather than overclaiming byte-identity. The two live internal-split rivals it names (the Sidon address shift, the disclosure-speech pair) are real, not strawmen.

items.claim: The restoration sub-oracle is correctly launched on its own fresh in-that-day interval formula, distinct from the preceding taunt-lament's voice, and closes cleanly at the chapter's own end.
items.evidence: Isa.23.15 opens on וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וְנִשְׁכַּ֤חַת צֹר֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה כִּימֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ אֶחָ֑ד מִקֵּ֞ץ שִׁבְעִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה לְצֹ֔ר כְּשִׁירַ֖ת הַזּוֹנָֽה, a fresh bayom-hahu clause introducing a seventy-year interval absent from the preceding material; the row closes at Isa.23.18's own consecration formula, disclosed as coinciding with but not driven by the chapter boundary. The seventy-year/one-king referent is correctly held open rather than resolved.

items.claim: The cosmic judgment unit is correctly bounded at its own third-person, addressee-less onset and runs in one continuous voice through its closing simile without a strong enough internal seam to justify a finer split.
items.evidence: Isa.24.1 opens הִנֵּ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה בּוֹקֵ֥ק הָאָ֖רֶץ וּבֽוֹלְקָ֑הּ וְעִוָּ֣ה פָנֶ֔יהָ וְהֵפִ֖יץ יֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ, a third-person judgment announcement with no addressee, distinct from the preceding restoration oracle's direct Tyre address; the remnant-root mentions inside the row's own span are correctly treated as in-unit texture. Re-derivation also tested the mid-span closing-style clause at Isa.24.3 (כִּ֣י יְהוָ֔ה דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶת הַדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה, 'for Yahweh has spoken this word') as a candidate internal seam; it carries no accompanying addressee or scene shift there and does not support a split, confirming the row's own choice to run through Isa.24.13.

items.claim: The two-verse praise-summons is correctly isolated on a genuine subject shift from the earth's judgment description to a third-person praising group, and the hymn_doxology deviation from the enumerated song sites is properly disclosed.
items.evidence: Isa.24.14 opens on the fronted pronoun in הֵ֛מָּה יִשְׂא֥וּ קוֹלָ֖ם יָרֹ֑נּוּ בִּגְא֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה צָהֲל֖וּ מִיָּֽם, marking a fresh subject distinct from the preceding earth-centered description; the operative-category deviation (applying hymn_doxology outside the enumerated song sites) carries the required one-sentence disclosure. The rejected merge-through-Isa.24.16 alternative correctly names the grammatical-person-plus-speech-act shift rather than a vaguer ground.

items.claim: The row honestly holds the Isa.24.16 voice slide at reduced confidence, but its rejected-alternative disclosure names only the narrower 'own row for v.16' rival and omits a broader one: a recurring inhabitant(s)-of-the-earth idiom that ties Isa.24.17-20 back to the chapter's own opening rather than only forward through the row's own span.
items.evidence: The lemma behind יֹשְׁבֶֽיהָ (Isa.24.1), תַּ֣חַת יֹשְׁבֶ֑יהָ (Isa.24.5), and יֹ֣שְׁבֵי בָ֑הּ / יֹ֣שְׁבֵי אֶ֔רֶץ (Isa.24.6) recurs at Isa.24.17's עָלֶ֖יךָ יוֹשֵׁ֥ב הָאָֽרֶץ, a lexical-tier (not byte-identical) recurrence naming the same referent class the row's own account of the chapter opening does not raise. This is weaker than a byte-true device and does not overturn the medium_low confidence already assigned to the row's own quoted material (א֣וֹי לִ֑י, בֹּגְדִ֣ים בָּגָ֔דוּ at Isa.24.16, both verified against the source), but the strongest real rival to this row's own span — that Isa.24.17-20 resumes the chapter's own opening judgment idiom rather than continuing as one voice with the Isa.24.16 lament — goes unnamed.
